problem.title: Per-coordinate fibered Weil-lift extension and jet transport
problem.user_statement: Notice that jet transport is not a property that must be satisfied by a method for all vector fields in a large enough class. ... [see LOG.md round 0 for full verbatim text] ... Notice that even though we can consider the two extensions R[eps_1]/(eps_1)^2 and R[eps_2]/eps_2^2 in each coordinate for a system of dimension 2 (and analogous for higher dimensions), these are actually the same algebra with distinct naming of the symbol. So, in the same way that one expects that changing the name of the variables in an ODE does not imply a change of the solution, only the same renaming of the variables in them, wouldn't we expect a method to satisfy that too? There is a great distinction in what a vector field accepts and what the method accepts. Notice that we are not trying to study vector fields, but actually if requiring this property as part of the machinery assumed by jet transport makes sense, and if so, how does this actually restrict the methods that satisfy such property.
problem.current_statement: Round 2 claim (Lilith Direction 1 from the r2-propose step): On coupled 2-dimensional vector fields under a per-coordinate fibered extension with equal per-coordinate Weil algebras W_1=W_2=R[e]/(e^2), require the lift to satisfy relabeling/renaming equivariance -- consistently swapping which coordinate is assigned which formal nilpotent symbol (simultaneously relabeling e_1<->e_2 together with x_1<->x_2) must commute with forming the lift. Test this hypothesis against the two candidate cross-term handling maps located in jt-percoord Round 1: (a) index-blind projection -- coordinate i's lift discards all nilpotent contributions from W_j, j!=i; (b) degree-truncation -- coordinate i's lift keeps only terms up to a fixed total nilpotent-degree bound across all W_j's. Does renaming-equivariance distinguish between (a) and (b), rule out one or both, or leave both compatible?
problem.intent: Test whether requiring a method to be invariant under renaming of formally-identical per-coordinate Weil-algebra symbols (analogous to ODE solutions being invariant under consistent variable renaming) is a sensible and non-vacuous hypothesis to add to jet-transport's machinery, and if so, how restrictive it is -- specifically whether it adjudicates between the two inequivalent cross-term gluing maps Round 1 located.
